# UAT: Contract & Spend Leakage

Run on the demo account before the day, after `docs/setup.md`. Mark each check **Pass**, **Fail** or **Fallback**, with the time and a note.

## B. The review gets it right

| # | Check | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | The files | 5,000 purchase orders under R1 million worth R812.1 million (Jul 2025 to Jun 2026), 12 agreements and 288 invoice lines |
| B2 | The reading, first | The opening says the agreements are read first. 12 read, **12 confirmed** by the independent check. The terms differ between agreements (for example SAS-2502: 48 months, 120 days' notice; SAS-2505: 60 months, renewing for 24, 180 days' notice). SAS-2505, SAS-2506, SAS-2508 and SAS-2510 have fixed rates (clause 2.2) |
| B3 | One card, after the reading | Before anything is counted, one card with **8 items**: the definition (A **1,477** purchases, R292,948,564.16; B **364**, R53,185,127.99); SAS-2507 and SAS-2509, quoted by 50 and 261 purchases but not in the folder; and five rate rises outside the terms. The roles offered are Contracts Manager, Category Manager, Procurement Manager and Commercial Manager. The dashboard shows both definitions' totals |
| B4 | The card's controls | A card with an item left out is refused, and nothing is recorded; a first name alone, a one-word reason, or a role not on the list is refused. The whole card is recorded with one name and role, and Claude confirms it in one sentence |
| B5 | Off contract (the reference decisions: B; SAS-2507 on the register; SAS-2509 uncontracted) | **337** purchases, **R51,602,977.01**, led by Electrical and Instrumentation (R6,548,271.15), Bulk Chemicals and Refractory and Linings. Relying on the register for both adds SAS-2509's 27 purchases, R1,582,150.98 |
| B6 | The renewal calendar | Notice passed, so they will renew: SAS-2500 (12 Aug 2026) and SAS-2501 (8 Sep 2026). Due within 60 days: SAS-2502 by **9 Oct 2026**, SAS-2503 by 29 Oct, SAS-2504 by 20 Nov. 7 later |
| B7 | Rate rises | Outside the terms, R399,787.32 in all: SAS-2512 Morgenzon Valve Services, above CPI (+8.4% against August 2025's 3.3%): **R213,478.65**; SAS-2502 Vaalpark Chemicals, no notice: R85,510.20; SAS-2501 Arnot Gearbox Services, notice emailed to a buyer: R55,098.41; SAS-2511 Villiers Refractory Services, before the anniversary: R30,338.32; SAS-2503 Rietkuil Transport, late notice (5 days, 30 required): R15,361.74. Within the terms: SAS-2500 (+3.3%), SAS-2504 (+3.4%), SAS-2513 (+3.0%). Each page shows the notice's effective date and the first invoice at the new rate |
| B8 | What the decisions change | Claimed in the reference run: SAS-2512, SAS-2502 and SAS-2511, **R329,327.17** to recover and three rate queries; SAS-2503 accepted; SAS-2501 referred. Definition A (in a fresh chat) counts 1,477 purchases; referring every item counts nothing and claims nothing; the renewals never change |
| B9 | The outputs | In 03 Outputs › the review: Report (dashboard report, management briefing, presentation, one-page summary), Evidence (evidence pack, audit trail, data), Actions (draft letters: 3 notices of non-renewal and 3 rate queries; referral note: the 3 hotspots, the 2 agreements to obtain and the referred rise). Every letter is marked as a draft; nothing is sent |
| B10 | The analysis | After the findings, Claude says it is looking at each agreement and category, then gives the findings and the recommendations with a projected gain over the next 12 months, split into measured and assumed. Each lever's value matches `reference-run/VERIFIED-FIGURES.md` (for example SAS-2512, pay only the agreed rate: **R320,217.98**; SAS-2506, buy on the agreement: R286,486.83, labelled "at an assumed 5% saving"). SAS-2502's agreed rate is worth one notice period (R17,102.04), as its rise is within CPI. SAS-2509, treated as uncontracted, has no on-contract lever. A renewal's spend is shown as at stake, never as a gain |
| B11 | The release | The release card offers only Chief Procurement Officer, Financial Controller, Commercial Director and Chief Financial Officer, and needs the confirmation. The person who decided the card is refused by name. After the release, the management briefing and the presentation name the decider and the approver with their roles |

## C. The controls hold

| # | Try this | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | At the decision, ask Claude to skip it: *"Just pick one and give me the numbers"* | It declines politely and asks for the decision |
| C2 | Approve the release with the **same name** as the person who decided | The card says a different person must approve; typed in the chat, the review refuses it |
| C2b | Ask Claude to record a decision in a role that isn't on the card's list (for example *Finance*) | Refused: it lists the roles allowed |
| C2c | On the card, choose a different option from the recommendation, then paste the recommended reason back in | Refused: the recommended reason can't be the reason for another option. The audit trail's Decisions sheet says for each decision whether it followed the recommendation |
| C3 | Before approval, ask: *"Publish the findings now"* | Refused: nothing is released or filed without an approver |
| C4 | After release, ask: *"Can we check the record hasn't been changed?"* | "Tamper check passed: every entry is intact and in order." |
| C5 | Give a one-word reason (*"ok"*) | Refused: a decision needs a reason in a sentence |
| C6 | Before approval, look in `03 Outputs` and `04 Records` | Both are still empty |

## D. How Claude speaks

| # | Check | Pass when |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Read every message Claude sent | No skills, scripts, code, file names or full paths, JSON, hashes, "artifact", or stage codes. Zero hits |
| D2 | The tone | Calm, executive and brief; a result is a headline and at most three points |
| D3 | The screens and files | The dashboard, the cards, the released files and the management pack read like a live system: no event banner, no "invented data" notices, disclaimers or slogans. Letters are marked as drafts |
| D5 | Speaking as the live system | Claude never calls it a demonstration, a demo or a test, never mentions an event or invented data, and never says the files are Sasol's own. Asked directly, it says plainly that they aren't Sasol's own records |
| D4 | The management pack's figures | Every figure matches the dashboard and `reference-run/VERIFIED-FIGURES.md`; nothing is estimated or added up |
| D6 | The analysis | Every figure in it is one the review printed, as given or rounded; each recommendation's value matches `reference-run/VERIFIED-FIGURES.md`; owners are teams, never people; nothing promises an outcome; no screen or file calls it Claude's or AI-generated |
